how: Calls mobilize members to defend the flag and place blue pixels against its perceived attackers.
A participant joins the Patriote build with a bare commitment, while an offered neighbour receives a bare thanks.
A proposal to organize a flag receives an unexplained refusal, so reason-giving cannot be assumed for every local rejection.
A willing newcomer needs an explanation of the canvas before participating, preserving the ladder's sensemaking step outside the standing processes.
A lower-pixel location away from Canadian interference is proposed as a constrained alternative rather than a measured count of available hands.
Reported exhaustion and relocation do not establish that insufficient hands caused the move.
The starter proposes a flag, maps its dimensions and reports having begun placing at an anchor coordinate.
Starting and recruiting occur in the same opening, so the local sequence does not require a separate later recruitment stage.
Members revise the initial flag through competing second-flag and Patriote proposals.
Members report apparent completion and avoidable repair work, including a refresh that reveals unrecorded placing.
The invitation precedes participation reports, but the record does not identify which placers joined because of that call.
Models, coordinates and gridded images align manual placers and script users around an actionable target.
Templates settle only a current target because friendly overwriting and later redesigns require renewed agreement.
Members share placement commands, loop the script and agree to synchronize target changes.
A revised target requires simultaneous script updates because otherwise automated placement fights the new design.
Proposed leadership and declared official strategy establish attempts to decide order, while friendly overwriting leaves effective collective command unresolved.
Moving deliberation into live chat addresses poor coordination on Reddit, a backstage decision step named in the ladder but missing from the standing processes.
Participants prioritize repair and defence, including leaving an automated placer running to hold the work.
Thanks for creation and protection accompany a border proposal explicitly responding to the advancing rainbow.
Greater efficiency and defensive script use are visible, but manual upkeep exceeding capacity as the cause of adoption remains unestablished.
A moderator accusation is corrected through an explanation of delayed pixel attribution and a response acknowledging premature blame.
Names require refreshing before they warrant attribution, and reasonable doubt can justify withdrawing an accusation list.
Participants report agreements to pass behind neighbouring drawings and propose conditional peace.
A speaker explicitly proposes peace because a named neighbour is eroding the B.
Explaining a memorial's meaning elicits an explicit agreement to spare it.
Restraint can follow recognition of a memorial's meaning without a previously settled border.
Members offer pixels to Nova Scotia and help Newfoundland after describing their own work as secure.
Own-work strain can inhibit outgoing help, while security of the home mark licenses it.
A request to spare neighbouring art receives agreement and a reciprocal request for help.
Announced alliances exchange protection of neighbouring icons for protection of the flag against Canada.
The stated alliance basis is complementary protection, without demonstrating that both partners already faced an identical threat.
Alliance obligations are invoked to stop attacks on an allied icon and refuse expansion.
An agreement reached through contact with another room is relayed alongside a route for further proposals.
A new-spot strategy and a retrospective account of tiring and moving aside document relocation.
Retrospective complaints about a flag inside another flag do not establish a host approval regime.
Distrust and alliance enforcement are recorded, but an explicit dispute over who can bind the room is not observed in the coded passages.
The alliance record does not show negotiation producing an explicit contest over representative authority.
Participants argue national belonging, invoke referendum investment and relate the pixel war to sovereignist history.
Historical framing cannot establish a pre-existing subreddit quarrel as the encounter's cause when a participant recounts beginning the small flag for fun.
Assimilation language directly motivates a protective call, but these coded passages do not establish inherited history naming the rival in the same attacking turn.
Political refusal can take the form of deliberately erasing one's own subordinate emblem while planning a larger replacement.
Canvas visibility brings a visitor back with political questions and elicits an explanation through pixel autonomy, without proving recruitment or conversion.
Members contest the post flood, obtain a megathread and enforce its rule against new attack and result posts.
Centralization is explicitly justified as leaving room for other subjects and followed by removal enforcement.
Ordinary attention adjusts through postponing news, reading during pixel waits and recruiting an existing nostalgia format.
Claims of collective unity must retain their participating constituency alongside explicit rejection, nonparticipation and doubts about real-world consequence.
Uncertainty about a placement bug being an April Fools trick does not establish a host-sub prank or takeover.
High-fives and final congratulations credit the participants and their surviving work.
Completion rituals mark provisional milestones while further lettering and defence remain active.
Participants write a timeline, document the effort in a wiki and report losses and the canvas's end.
Congratulating and mourning can occur in one passage, so a separate celebration-causes-recording mechanism cannot be inferred from sequence alone.
Flag workers announce a general-purpose Discord to keep contact and later describe its everyday conversation.
Continuity is reported before shutdown, while the edited founding post's timestamp cannot independently date its founding passage.
The stated reason for continuing ties is shared labour and wanting contact, not the prior preservation of a finished image.
Working together is explicitly given as the reason for keeping contact while canvas activity continues.
Contact over canvas help opens a proposed cultural exchange and an invitation beyond the event.
Announcements and a later participant report establish intended continuity while long-term membership and persistence remain unresolved.
Post-close retelling and final-image appreciation do not show a dispute over which shared copy or historical version should be preserved.
Attacks include altering the Canadian lettering and proposing conversion of its flag into a fleurdelisé.
Recruitment and attack are interwoven, but the coded record does not establish that the former caused particular members to attack.
Threats, boasts of deceiving the enemy and retrospective blame carry the contest in talk.
The account supports participants' narrated contest but cannot independently verify their attribution of the rival's motives.
A warning that damaging others diverts effort from defence receives an agreement to concentrate on repair.
Attack and agreement are recorded, but these passages do not establish a causal transition to a deal with the same neighbour.
A call issued after shutdown remains an attack proposal without placement capacity, and its removal explicitly cites the finished event.
Canvas lettering becomes a contested subreddit name, prompting claims of ownership and a proposed reclamation through the platform's request channel.
Requests for incoming help are visible, but a shortage of hands causing those requests is not established by the coded passages.
